correctness.rationale: Circulant discrete Fourier diagonalization of the positive definite kernel G yields each nonzero frequency of optimal w equal to that of the tent density masses q_j via the csc-square aliasing identity. Their difference is a common scalar fixed by the zero Fourier mode: w_j=q_j-gamma(B-A)/[n(1+gamma B)]. The folded half-period convolution has its minimum at the density zero j=0 by symmetry, unimodality and circular layer-cake rearrangement; q0=1/2−n sin(2pi/n)/(4pi). Consequently positivity cuts off sharply at Gamma_pos=n q0/(B−A−n q0 B), with exact equality zero; sum w=(1+gamma A)/(1+gamma B) switches at Gamma_mass=−1/A. A<0 follows explicit summands. The n=2 equality and strict n>=3 ordering follow algebra, and Taylor expansions give order-n versus order-n^4 thresholds. Independent high-precision, separately integrated kernel-mean/Gram solves for n=2,3,4,5,7 and gamma in {0.1,3.7} reproduced formulas; analytic proof is required for all n.
